goal: Determine and then enable the smallest coverage-complete, source-addressable Anime.js v4 knowledge vault that agents can consult while working, including the complete official documentation topology, API semantics, examples, migration boundaries, task recipes, pitfalls, repair lessons, and an evidence-bound contract for accumulating future agent work lessons. The result must support a private candidate-local ontology package without copying the documentation verbatim or claiming authority beyond its official sources.
context: The current official documentation exposes Getting started, Timer, Animation, Timeline, Animatable, Draggable, Layout, Scope, Events, SVG, Text, Utilities, Easings, WAAPI, Engine, and Adapters, while the official juliangarnier/anime repository provides source, types, tests, examples, releases, and a v3 migration guide. Recent local ontology work provides several candidate package patterns, but the active Inventory has no Anime.js entry and its coverage of fresh untracked ontology work is incomplete. Research outputs land only in this working folder; after an accepted audit, the parent may use Ontology Vault to build projects/animejs/ontology/agent-knowledge-vault/ as a private candidate-local package with authority_effect none and release_admission not-granted.
anti_bias_global: Coverage completeness versus semantic restraint: official documentation and runtime facts, local ontology precedent, and agent-learning utility must cross-check one another without turning source indexes, examples, or work episodes into unsupported truth.

groups.anti_bias: Composite source-corpus and methodology axis: official documentation topology, local ontology-model precedent, and evidence-bound agent-work lessons.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs a computational official-documentation coverage crawl while agent 1 runs a historical-lineage survey of recent local ontology packages on the source-corpus and methodology axes; a bias in agent 0 toward mirroring site navigation would be exposed by agent 1's typed package and validation requirements, while a bias in agent 1 toward reusing local machinery would be exposed by agent 0's exact Anime.js topic and API coverage gaps.

Agent 0 runs page, API, example, and version coverage while agent 2 runs task-centered agent consultation and lesson-capture analysis on the methodology axis; a bias in agent 0 toward treating documentation facts as sufficient guidance would be exposed by agent 2's failure-and-repair episodes, while a bias in agent 2 toward anecdotal advice would be exposed by agent 0's official source bindings.

Agent 1 runs recent ontology schema, relation, view, and validator precedent while agent 2 runs operational recipe, pitfall, and lesson-evidence design on the source-corpus and methodology axes; a bias in agent 1 toward structure without use would be exposed by agent 2's query and work-episode witnesses, while a bias in agent 2 toward a loose tips collection would be exposed by agent 1's typed provenance and non-authority constraints.

agents.angle: Computational official-source coverage: enumerate the live Anime.js v4 documentation tree, API objects, parameters, methods, examples, guides, migration boundaries, releases, source modules, type declarations, and tests with exact selectors.
agents.initial_prompt: Use only current primary Anime.js sources: https://animejs.com/documentation/ and its complete descendant documentation pages, https://github.com/juliangarnier/anime, repository releases/tags, the official v3-to-v4 migration guide, and official source/types/tests/examples at a pinned commit. Produce a coverage manifest rather than a prose dump. For every page or API topic return canonical URL, heading or structured selector, topic kind, module/export, concepts, parameters, returns, related topics, examples, version boundary, and observed/unverified status. Identify every documentation section omitted by the initial root navigation, redirects, duplicates, badges or JS-versus-WAAPI distinctions, and stale-version risks. Do not copy whole pages, rely on community summaries, or edit files. Return exact-binding rows suitable for a source manifest and graph coverage validator. Use only the official-source and gap fields from strategy-inventory-packet.json.

agents.angle: Historical-lineage and formal precedent: inspect all recent locally created ontology models selected by Inventory plus live recent-model gaps, and extract reusable package, node, relation, evidence, view, query, validator, and receipt patterns.
agents.initial_prompt: Read strategy-inventory-packet.json first, then inspect the selected recent ontology packages and their exact current source artifacts: projects/augmentor/ontology/unified-agent/, projects/domainspec-v2/development/implementation-conformance/ontology-experiment/, projects/domainspec-v2/development/implementation-conformance/unified-ontology-canvas/ when present, projects/body-war/ontology/business/, cyberAlchemy-v2/implementation/ontology-candidate-graph-prototype/, the 2026-08-01 learning-graph research result, and the 2026-08-02 tower exam graph seed/review. Reconcile Inventory with live git/filesystem evidence so fresh untracked or candidate-local artifacts are not silently omitted. Return one manifest row per genuinely created model, distinguishing ontology package, generated view, research proposal, and learning projection. Extract reusable shapes and anti-patterns for Anime.js: source records, concept nodes, typed relations, provenance, evidence status, views, queries, lessons, validators, fixtures, digests, receipts, and non-authority ceilings. Do not mutate any existing ontology or treat Inventory as proof.

agents.angle: Empirical agent-knowledge utility: derive task recipes, prerequisite paths, pitfalls, repair patterns, version traps, and an append-only work-episode-to-lesson contract grounded in official docs, source, tests, and bounded examples.
agents.initial_prompt: Using official Anime.js documentation, the pinned official repository source/types/tests/examples, and official issue/release history only as explicitly classified evidence, design how an agent should consult and extend the knowledge vault while implementing animations. Separate source-derived guidance, code-derived facts, test-observed behavior, executed local witness evidence, inference, and unverified community proposal. Treat GitHub issue #1105 as unadmitted precedent to verify, not official guidance. Return task recipes for setup/imports, animation, timelines, scopes/framework cleanup, draggable/layout, events, SVG/text, utilities/easings, WAAPI choice, engine/adapters, debugging, performance, accessibility/reduced motion, and v3 migration where official evidence exists. Define WorkEpisode, Task, Attempt, Symptom, Diagnosis, Fix, Outcome, Lesson, Evidence, VersionContext, and their typed relations/invalidation rules. Include positive, failed, stale-version, and abstention examples; do not invent lessons or run destructive/networked product integrations.

Reconcile the three explorer returns into one exact-bound Anime.js agent knowledge-vault blueprint. Produce: a complete official-source coverage manifest; a disposition of every recent local ontology/model precedent; ontology type selection knowledge-vault with competing types excluded; node and relation catalogs; source, version, evidence, lesson, invalidation, and ownership fields; agent query contracts; task-recipe and prerequisite paths; source-derived versus operational lesson separation; human-readable views; deterministic coverage and graph validation; positive, negative, stale-version, and abstention fixtures; copyright-safe paraphrase rules; update and drift protocol; and an exact artifact tree for projects/animejs/ontology/agent-knowledge-vault/. Every load-bearing row must carry immutable source identity, exact selector or structured pointer, explorer return reference, evidence scope, and observed, executed, inferred, or unverified status. Preserve disagreements and do not write repository files.

groups.anti_bias: Attack-vector axis: precedent ownership, non-vacuity agent-query witnesses, and definitional plus evidence non-collapse.

predicted_disagreements.statement: Agent 0 runs the precedent and ownership gate while agent 1 runs finite agent-query and repair-witness pressure on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward declaring the vault already owned would be exposed when existing models cannot answer an Anime.js work question, while a bias in agent 1 toward new machinery would be exposed when a recent package already owns the required structure.

Agent 0 runs duplicate-owner and prior-art classification while agent 2 runs definitional, evidence, version, and authority-collapse attacks on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 0 toward wholesale reuse would be exposed by agent 2 when documentation, code, examples, lessons, and authority are conflated, while a bias in agent 2 toward proliferating types would be exposed by agent 0 when an existing primitive already owns the distinction.

Agent 1 runs concrete setup, implementation, debugging, migration, stale-version, and abstention witnesses while agent 2 runs tautology and source-to-lesson non-collapse attacks on the attack-vector axis; a bias in agent 1 toward a persuasive recipe would be exposed when advice lacks evidence or invalidation, while a bias in agent 2 toward semantic purity would be exposed when a distinct relation changes an agent's next action observably.

agents.angle: Precedent gate: verify every reuse claim against recent local ontology packages and official Anime.js agent-guidance precedent, classifying build-from-owned versus genuinely new work.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply only the precedent gate to the synthesized blueprint. Verify live source artifacts behind every Inventory lead and every claimed recent ontology model. Check official Anime.js documentation/repository precedent, including issue #1105 only as unadmitted proposal evidence. Classify each artifact, node, relation, query, lesson contract, view, and validator as already-deployed, build-from-owned, proposed, deferred, or precedent-clean; being owned never emits KILL. Identify duplicate owners and exact reuse constraints. Reject novelty claims based on Inventory no-match and route missing source evidence only through the confirmed synthesizer-to-explorers feedback edge.

agents.angle: Non-vacuity and counter-example gate: force the graph to answer finite Anime.js implementation, debugging, migration, and lesson-update questions with observable distinctions and safe abstention.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply the non-vacuity gate. Hand-execute queries for at least: selecting JS animate versus WAAPI, composing a timeline, cleaning up a framework scope, debugging a v3/v4 name mismatch, choosing an SVG helper, recording a failed attempt and verified fix, invalidating a lesson after a version change, and abstaining when accessibility/performance or runtime evidence is absent. Add mutants for missing source, stale version, conflicting docs/code, copied prose, circular prerequisites, decorative relations, unverified issue advice, and a lesson with no work episode. KILL any primitive that cannot change retrieval, explanation, next action, diagnosis, validation, invalidation, or abstention. Return exact binding gaps and expected decisions.

agents.angle: Definitional and evidence gate: attack collapse among documentation topic, API symbol, source fact, example, recipe, attempt, outcome, lesson, inference, recommendation, version, and ontology authority.
agents.initial_prompt: Apply the definitional-soundness gate. Require every surviving node and relation to have a distinct invariant, endpoint types, direction, evidence class, invalidation rule, owner route, and misuse warning. Test whether the proposed vault is more than a copied site index or generic RAG corpus; whether a Lesson is distinguishable from documentation guidance and an Attempt; whether an example proves behavior; whether an issue is official guidance; whether current-version facts can be generalized across releases; and whether graph validation is kept separate from semantic truth, accessibility, performance, and production readiness. Return KEEP, MERGE, RENAME, DEFER, or KILL with exact citations and the smallest repaired vocabulary.

Write findings.md only from the evidence-closed synthesis and reviewer receipts. State the direct answer; enumerate all genuinely created recent local ontology/model precedents and what is reused; specify the Anime.js source corpus and coverage contract; define the complete node/relation/evidence/version/lesson/query/view model; give the exact candidate package tree; include task recipes, positive/negative/stale/abstention witnesses, validation commands and pass/fail signals, copyright-safe source handling, update/drift flow, verdict matrix, risks, non-goals, claim ceiling, and the bounded Ontology Vault handoff. Every load-bearing claim must cite explorer evidence. Do not write research.md, the ontology package, Inventory, existing ontology files, ledger, Git, publication, release, or promotion state.

Audit findings.md only against the frozen goal and exact-binding contract. Require complete official documentation-topic disposition, pinned official repository/version evidence, an honest complete list of recent local ontology models versus research proposals/views, a usable agent query and work-lesson model, distinct source/evidence/version/lesson semantics, executable deterministic validator and fixture plans, copyright-safe paraphrase and source links, explicit stale-version handling, and non-authority claim ceilings. Reject copied documentation, invented selectors, issue comments treated as official guidance, unverified lessons presented as learned, omitted topic families, duplicate ownership, or claims of semantic truth, accessibility, performance, publication, release, deployment, or production readiness. Return ACCEPT or one bounded writer revision list.
